blocks.title: After this PDF you can
bullets: choose between the preterite and the imperfect in most everyday situations
tell a short story with background (imperfect) and events (preterite)
combine both tenses in one sentence (Cocinaba cuando sonó el teléfono)
explain why saber, conocer, querer and poder change meaning

blocks.text: Both tenses talk about the past. The difference is how you look at it. The preterite moves the story forward: it says what happened. The imperfect paints the scene: it says what things were like or what used to happen.

head: Preterite
Imperfect
rows: Scenery, background, what was going on
A finished moment or a finished period
No beginning or end in view
Once or a counted number of times
I always used to eat paella.

blocks.title: Dutch toen can be either
blocks.text: Toen ik jong was describes a state: Cuando era joven. Toen ik aankwam is a single event: Cuando llegué. Same Dutch word, different Spanish tense. Ask yourself what the verb after toen describes.

head: Usually preterite
Usually imperfect
rows: el lunes, el 5 de mayo, en 2019
la semana pasada, el año pasado
una vez, dos veces, muchas veces (counted)

blocks.title: Clues help, but meaning decides
blocks.text: Time words are strong hints, not absolute rules. When a sentence has no time word, or the clue is unclear, ask the questions in section 5.
In a story, the imperfect sets the scene and the preterite pushes the action on. Read this example and look at the reason for each tense.

head: Sentence
Tense
Why
rows: Era sábado y hacía mucho calor.
Yo estaba en casa y leía un libro.
a state and an action in progress
Me dijo que quería ir a la playa.

blocks.text: It was Saturday and it was very hot. I was at home reading a book. Suddenly the phone rang. It was my friend Marta. She told me she wanted to go to the beach. I got my things ready and left.
4. An action interrupted, or two actions at once

head: Pattern
Example
English
rows: I was cooking when the phone rang.
When I arrived, my mother was cooking.
Mientras yo comía, ella veía la tele.
While I was eating, she was watching TV.
I arrived, ate and went to bed.

blocks.title: The rule of thumb
blocks.text: The long, ongoing action takes the imperfect. The short interrupting action takes the preterite.

items: Did it happen once and finish (or a counted number of times)? Preterite.
Did it happen again and again, or can you say used to? Imperfect.
Is it a description: age, time, weather, feelings, how someone looked? Imperfect.
Is it a list of actions in order (first this, then that)? Preterite.
Is it in progress when something else happened? Imperfect for the background, preterite for the interruption.

head: Verb
Imperfect (state)
Preterite (event)
rows: Supe la respuesta. (I found it out.)
Quise irme. (I tried / decided to leave.)
No podía abrir la puerta. (I could not open it.)
No pude abrir la puerta. (I tried and failed.)
Estaba en Madrid. (I was in Madrid.)
Estuve en Madrid tres días. (I spent three days in Madrid.)

blocks.text: The same logic works for description versus summary: La fiesta era genial (it was great while I was there) and La fiesta fue genial (looking back, it was a great party).

blocks.title: Today and this week in Spain
blocks.text: With hoy, esta mañana, esta semana and este año, Spain normally uses the present perfect (next PDF), not either of these tenses: Hoy he comido tarde. With ayer, anoche or la semana pasada, use the preterite.

rows: Cuando era niño, fui al parque cada día.
Cuando era niño, iba al parque cada día.
A habit in the past: imperfect.
Two actions in progress at the same time: both imperfect.
Her cooking was in progress when I arrived: imperfect.
El año pasado íbamos a Italia.
El año pasado fuimos a Italia.
One finished trip with a time marker: preterite.
Conocía a Marta ayer en la fiesta.
Conocí a Marta ayer en la fiesta.
Meeting someone for the first time: preterite.
Eran las ocho cuando él llegaba.
Eran las ocho cuando él llegó.
The time is background; the arrival is the event.
A habit in the past: imperfect.

blocks.text: Write the verb in the preterite or the imperfect. Answers are on the last page.

items.q: Cuando era niño, ______ en la calle.
items.full: Cuando era niño, jugaba en la calle.

items.q: Mientras ella ______, yo veía la tele.
items.full: Mientras ella estudiaba, yo veía la tele.
El año pasado viajaron a Japón.

items.q: De pequeño, siempre ______ en casa de mi abuela.
items.full: De pequeño, siempre comía en casa de mi abuela.

items.q: Ella ______ quince años cuando se mudó a Madrid.
items.full: Ella tenía quince años cuando se mudó a Madrid.

items.q: When I arrived, it was raining.
Last summer we went to Cádiz.
items.a: El verano pasado fuimos a Cádiz.

items.q: While I was cooking, she called me.
As a child he never ate fish.
